title: Axes, handedness and units checker and converter for glTF
purpose: Diagnose a glTF that is Z-up, mirrored or in the wrong unit (checked against expected dimensions and triangle winding) and convert it between up axes, handedness, front-face winding and units, transforming nodes, meshes, skins and animations.

entry_points.name: conversion
entry_points.signature: conversion(source, target='gltf', unit_m=1.0, target_unit_m=1.0) -> (Q, k, flip)

entry_points.name: convert_document
entry_points.signature: convert_document(asset, Q, k, flip) -> glTF document with one embedded buffer

entry_points.name: winding_agreement
entry_points.signature: winding_agreement(asset) -> share of triangles that wind with their normals

entry_points.name: convert
entry_points.signature: convert(source_path, target_path, source, target='gltf', unit_m=1.0, expected=None, tolerance=0.005) -> asset_report.Report

entry_points.name: main
entry_points.usage: python3 axes_units_converter.py check ASSET.gltf --expect-dimensions X Y Z | convert IN.gltf OUT.gltf --from CONVENTION [--to CONVENTION] [--unit-m U]

inputs.name: expect-dimensions
inputs.format: the scene box size in metres along glTF X, Y and Z

inputs.name: conventions
inputs.format: gltf (+Y up, +Z front, right-handed, counter-clockwise), z_up_right (+Z up, -Y front, right-handed, counter-clockwise), y_up_left_cw, z_up_left_cw

report.subject: the checked or written file name
report.ok: true when the measurements match the expectation and triangles wind with their normals
report.failures: list of {code, where, detail with the conversion that repairs it}
report.facts: dimensions_m, bounds_m, tallest_axis, winding_agreement; after convert also converted_from, matrix, unit_factor, mirrored, winding_reversed

contract.proves: check: the scene box equals the expected dimensions within tolerance, or the report names the axis swap or uniform unit factor that explains it, and at least half of the triangles wind with their stored normals. convert: every node transform, vertex attribute, morph target, inverse bind matrix and animation output is mapped by the same change of basis and unit, so world geometry keeps its shape in the new convention.
contract.does_not_prove: Which way the asset should face (forward is a declaration, not something measured), that cameras and lights still look the right way (their local -Z convention is not corrected), or that quantized data converts (it is refused).

limits: Conventions are signed axis permutations with a uniform unit factor; arbitrary rotations are not offered. Quantized (integer) positions, normals or animation outputs are refused. Sparse accessors become dense, interleaved data becomes tightly packed, and every buffer is embedded in the output. Cameras and lights keep their node transform change but get no correction rotation. Winding agreement needs stored normals. The diagnosis recognises one axis swap or one uniform unit factor, not combinations.
technique_references: Change of basis by conjugation: M L M^-1 for node transforms
Quaternion of Q R Q^T for a signed axis permutation: the axis is a pseudovector
Triangle winding against vertex normals as a mirroring test
glTF 2.0 specification: +Y up, +Z front, metres, right-handed
